This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 03.03.2020 passed by XIX Additional Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru (for short 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.6206/2017.

entities.text: XIX Additional Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation.
Hence, the appellant seeks enhancement of compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.

At that time, the driver of tractor and trailer bearing registration Nos.KA-07-T- NC: 2024:KHC:1937 3177 and AP-26-AA-1527 drove the said vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle of the claimant.
Due to the impact of the said accident, claimant fell down and sustained injuries.
Immediately, he was shifted to R.L.Jalappa Hospital, Kolar, where he took treatment as an inpatient for 39 days and discharged with an advise to take follow up treatment.
Hence, the claimant filed a claim petition seeking compensation.

3.1 On service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through their counsel and filed statement of objections denied the claim made in the claim petition, disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident and sought for dismissal of the claim petition on the ground that proper and necessary parties are not made to the petition.
It also pleaded that the negligence was on the part of the rider of the motor cycle and hence, pleaded for dismissal of claim petition.
3.2 On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

sentences.text: In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, claimant got examined himself as PW.1 and the NC: 2024:KHC:1937 Doctor as PW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P16.

On the other hand, respondent No.2 examined its official as RW.1 and got marked documents as Exs.R1 and R2.
3.4

On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.4,54,100/- with interest 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit and also held that respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the claimant and respondent No.2 being the insurer was directed to deposit the amount within two months.
3.5
Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.

4. It is the vehement contention of the learned counsel for appellant-claimant that the tribunal has committed an error in not awarding just and reasonable compensation, ignored the material evidence on record and not assessed proper income of the claimant so also committed an error by reducing the NC: 2024:KHC:1937 percentage of disability expressed by PW.2-Doctor.
He also contended that on other heads also, the tribunal has awarded meager compensation, which calls for interference.
Accordingly, he seeks to allow the appeal preferred by the claimant and seeks enhancement of compensation.

5. Per contra, learned counsel representing Insurance Company vehemently contends that there is no error or illegality committed by the tribunal and has awarded just and reasonable compensation on the basis of the material evidence placed on record.
He further contends that there is no interference called for at the hands of this Court.
Therefore, on these grounds, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.

6. Having heard learned counsel for appellant-claimant and learned counsel for respondent-Insurance Company, perused the impugned judgment and award, it is not in dispute that on 04.07.2017 while the claimant was riding his motor cycle, the tractor and trailer dashed against the motor cycle of the claimant leading to the injuries suffered by the claimant.

In order to substantiate these aspects, the claimant has produced the documents as Exs.P1 to P16, out of which,
Exs.P1 to P6 are NC: 2024:KHC:1937 the police records and Exs.P7 to P16 are the medical records from the hospital having taken the treatment.

The police records evidence the facts that the negligence is rightly attributed against the driver of the tractor and trailer and the medical records depicts the injuries sustained by the claimant in the road traffic accident.
The income taken by the tribunal is Rs.7,500/- per month as notional income, no documentary proof is produced before the tribunal to show the income.
However, the notional income chart of the Legal Services Authority prescribes the income of Rs.11,000/- for the accident of the year 2017.
Accordingly, income is taken as Rs.11,000/-.
The age of the claimant was 20 years at the time of accident.
The tribunal has rightly applied the multiplier at '18', which does not call for interference.

sentences.text: PW.2-Doctor has opined that there is disability of 15% to the whole body and 45% to the right lower limb, whereas the tribunal has assessed the disability to be 10% to the whole body.
I am in agreement with the learned counsel for appellant-claimant that the PW.2-Doctor has opined disability to an extent of 15%.

In order to reduce it or modify it, the tribunal will have to place reliance on cogent material placed on NC: 2024:KHC:1937 record or any contra material which would disprove the opinion expressed by PW.2-Doctor.
In the present case, there are no such thing placed before the tribunal to reduce the percentage of disability from 15% to 10%.
Under the circumstances, I am in agreement with the learned counsel for the appellant- claimant that disability has to be assessed at 15% rather 10%.
Therefore, the loss of future earing capacity due to disability would be Rs.3,56,400/- (Rs.11000/- x 12 x 18 x 15%) as against Rs.1,62,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
8. The tribunal has awarded Rs.45,000/- towards pain and suffering.
I deem it appropriate to award an additional amount of Rs.10,000/-.
In all, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.55,000/- under this head.
9. The tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities.
I deem it appropriate to award an additional amount of Rs.25,000/-.
In all, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.45,000/- under this head.
10. Towards nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges, Rs.40,000/- is awarded by the tribunal, which does not call for interference.
Towards medical expenses, Rs.1,64,600/- is awarded by the tribunal on the basis of actual bills produced by the claimant, which also does not call for interference.
12. Towards loss of income during laid up period, the tribunal has awarded Rs.22,500/-.
In view of enhancement of the income by this Court to Rs.11,000/- per month, the claimant would require atleast four months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore, claimant would be entitled to Rs.44,000/- (Rs.11,000/- x 4) under the head loss of income during laid up period.

13. In view of the above, the claimant would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,05,000/- as against Rs.4,54,100/- as mentioned in the table below:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
Pain and sufferings 55,000-00

Loss of amenities 45,000-00 Nourishment, conveyance and 40,000-00 attendant charges Medical expenses 1,64,600-00 Loss of future earning capacity 3,56,400-00 due to disability Loss of income during laid up 44,000-00 Sri.
